To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the trigger factor is a ribosome-associated chaperone and that it can bind simultaneously to the ribosome and to the nascent protein chain, thus facilitating its folding.

the trigger factor is a highly conserved ribosomal chaperone that binds to the ribosome in an identical manner in all three domains of life, that the binding of the trigger factor to the ribosome is not dependent on the presence of the nascent chain, and that the trigger factor and the signal-recogition particle can coexist on the ribosome.

TF interacts differently with the ribosome than previously thought, the hydrophobic crevices of TF and SRP can simultaneously accommodate nascent chains, and that TF and SRP may interact directly with each other.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of translation and protein folding in prokaryotes.
the mechanism of protein folding, the role of the ribosome in this mechanism, and the role of the SRP.
understanding the molecular mechanism of translation initiation and the regulation of gene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TF-ribosome interaction is highly specific and that the binding mode is determined by the sequence and structure of the ribosomal proteins.
the binding mode of TF to the ribosome is different from the previously published one.
the TF-ribosome interface is not conserved between eubacteria and archaea.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ribosome is a complex and dynamic molecular machine, which has the capacity for a wide range of functions, including the folding and targeting of nascent proteins.
the TF is a highly flexible and adaptable protein, which may account for its ubiquitous nature.
the TF-ribosome interface is highly conserved and that the TF-23S rRNA interactions are more extensive than previously thought.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TF is an integral part of the ribosome and is likely to play a key role in protein synthesis and folding.
the binding mode of TF on the ribosome is highly variable and that this variability may be important to its function.
TF is not a passive bystander during translation, but a dynamic player in the translation process.
